text: Near the village. <break time="0.8s" /> Lived a lady, a small landowner. <break time="0.8s" /> Who owned about three hundred acres. <break time="0.8s" /> She hired an old soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> As her manager. <break time="0.8s" /> Who fined the peasants. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever their animals wandered onto her fields. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom paid many fines. <break time="0.8s" /> And each time he went home. <break time="0.8s" /> In a bad temper. <break time="0.8s" /> Shouting at his family. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the news came. <break time="0.8s" /> That the lady wanted to sell her land. <break time="0.8s" /> And the peasants all wished to buy some. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the Devil made them quarrel. <break time="0.8s" /> They could not buy it together. <break time="0.8s" /> So each man bought what he could. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom sold a colt and half of his bees. <break time="0.8s" /> Borrowed money from his brother in law. <break time="0.8s" /> And bought forty acres. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom was full of joy. <break time="0.8s" /> On the day when he first plowed his own fields. <break time="0.8s" /> And even the grass looked different. <break time="0.8s" /> But soon the neighbors cattle. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to stray into his meadows. <break time="0.8s" /> And Pahom began to take their owners to court. <break time="0.8s" /> Once he had been the poor man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who paid fines. <break time="0.8s" /> But now he was the one. <break time="0.8s" /> Who made others pay. <break time="0.8s" /> His neighbors grew angry. <break time="0.8s" /> And when someone cut down his lime trees. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom blamed a peasant named Simon. <break time="0.8s" /> Without any proof.
